newsitem.title: USA: Motorola profits hurt by charge for dropping DRAMs.
newsitem.headline: Motorola profits hurt by charge for dropping DRAMs.

text.p: Technology giant Motorola Inc. on Tuesday reported a 10 percent sales gain for the second quarter but said its profits were hurt by a $170 million charge for phasing out its dynamic random access memory chip business.

It said it earned $268 million, or 44 cents per share, in the period, compared with profits of $326 million, or 54 cents per share, a year earlier. Revenues rose to $7.5 billion from $6.8 billion a year earlier.

Motorola Chief Executive Christopher Galvin said that following its exit from the DRAM business, the company will continue to review its operations and focus on those businesses that show the most potential.
"The potential for further actions could result in additional charges against earnings in the second half of the year," Galvin said.

Each of the company's business segments reported increased sales and orders, Robert Growney, president and chief operating officer, said in a statement. "Excluding the effect of the second-quarter charge ... we achieved increased profitability on a quarter-to-quarter basis versus the prior year."
Motorola's stock added $2.125 to $82.50 in aftermarket trading.
